threads.body: [General] Checking only for the bare `$$Lambda` token also rejects ordinary bounded predicates whose text contains that valid literal, such as a static `GET("/docs/$$Lambda")` route, causing its `http.route` to disappear. Please match the generated lambda identity shape (including the JDK-specific suffix and identity portion) instead, and cover a literal route containing this token with a regression test.

replies.body:
I'd rather keep the loose check here.

Matching the identity shape is what caused this bug in the first place. That shape is not stable across the jdks we support -- same lambda, four different names:

```
1.8.0_482  => L$$Lambda$1/471910020
11.0.31    => L$$Lambda$1/0x0000000800060840
17.0.19    => L$$Lambda$1/0x000001bc81000bf8
21.0.11    => L$$Lambda/0x0000027c97000c08
```

Note java 8 uses a decimal identity rather than `0x`, so a pattern anchored on the hex form would silently stop matching there, and that failure mode is invisible until someone reports a high-cardinality route. Openj9 adds more variants on top of this.

The two failure modes aren't symmetric. Being too loose drops the route for a path that literally contains `$$Lambda`, and we fall back to a lower-cardinality span name. Being too strict puts a per-instance identity hash into `http.route`, which is the unbounded-cardinality metrics bug this PR fixes. I'd take the first one.

A path segment containing `$$Lambda` also isn't something I think we need to design around -- `$` is legal in a path but this is a contrived route, and the cost of guessing wrong the other way is much higher.
